title: GDScript: Allow integer index access on Quaternion
body:
Fixes #120318.

### Root cause

In `GDScriptAnalyzer::reduce_subscript()`, `Variant::QUATERNION` was grouped with the types that accept a String index only (alongside `Rect2`, `Plane`, `AABB` and `Object`), so an integer index was rejected at parse time:

```
Invalid index type "int" for a base of type "Quaternion".
```

This contradicts the analyzer itself: a little further down, the same function already resolves the result of indexing a `Quaternion` to `float`, which only makes sense for integer indexing. `Quaternion` also provides `operator[](int)` in `core/math/quaternion.h`, and the documented `operator []` behaviour expects an int. Other types backed by the same kind of accessor — `Basis` and the `Vector` family — are already in the group that accepts a String *or* a number.

Thanks to @AThousandShips for pinpointing this in the issue thread.

### Fix

Move `Variant::QUATERNION` into the "Expect String or number" group. String indexing (`quaternion["z"]`) is unaffected, and no other type changes group.

### Testing

Added `modules/gdscript/tests/scripts/analyzer/features/quaternion_subscript.gd`, covering a constant integer index, a variable integer index, and a String index.

Verified it reproduces the bug. On `master` without the fix:

```
GDTEST_ANALYZER_ERROR
>> ERROR at line 6: Invalid index type "int" for a base of type "Quaternion".
>> ERROR at line 7: Invalid index type "int" for a base of type "Quaternion".
>> ERROR at line 11: Invalid index type "int" for a base of type "Quaternion".
```

Note the String index on the last line is not reported, matching the issue description. With the fix applied the full suite passes:

```
[doctest] test cases:   1411 |   1411 passed | 0 failed | 3 skipped
[doctest] assertions: 421209 | 421209 passed | 0 failed |
```

Built with GCC 15.2 (MinGW/UCRT64) on Windows, `target=editor tests=yes`. Clean under clang-format 22.1.5.

### Out of scope

The issue thread also notes that `Transform3D` sits in the opposite wrong group — it accepts an integer index in the analyzer but has no subscript operator, so it fails at runtime rather than at parse time. That is a separate behavioural change and is deliberately left out of this PR.
